Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are vulnerable to a range of evolving attacks including Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI). Abstract: Indirect prompt injection (IPI) attacks have emerged as a critical security threat to large language model (LLM)-based email agents. Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) models such as large language models (LLM) have demonstrated substantial advancements in recent years. These risks encompass reflective bias, toxic outputs, factually incorrect information, and adversarial outputs. However, in these existing works the focus has primarily been on the assessment of AI models not on the analysis of adversarial use-cases of these models. Red teaming research has focused in considerable depth on the adversarial use-case of conventional AI models, however very few works explore in detail the game-theoretic aspects of the red-teaming task for LLMs. LLMs can provide responses to questions posed in natural language, necessitating exploration of ways in which uncommon or non-obvious questions could be generated. In this work, a novel red teaming game framework (RTG) for LLMs and the Game-Theoretic Red Teaming System (GRTS) solver to balance the textual LLM policies is proposed. GRTS is guaranteed to converge to a Nash equilibrium (NE) when inner iterations converge and also incorporates lie detection for robustness against gradient leakage.
